questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Who founded a reformist organisation called ‘Brahmo Samaj’ in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born on **May 22, 1772, in Radhanagar, Hooghly District, Bengal**
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was **founded in 1828** by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• The Brahmo Samaj advocates belief in a **Monotheism, "Infinite Singularity"** that is infinite, indivisible, imperceptible, and indefinable.
 
• It promoted women's education and upliftment,** abolition of **social practices such as **Sati, child marriage, and the caste system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was born on September 26, 1820, in Birsingha village, West Bengal.
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a staunch** advocate for gender equality and the upliftment of women in society**.
 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was born on September 11, 1895, in Gagode village, Raigad, Maharashtra.
 
• In 1951, Vinoba Bhave started the **Bhoodan (land gift) movement**,
 
• He was awarded the** Ramon Magsaysay Award** for Community Leadership in 1958.
 
• **Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule** was Born on April 11, 1827, in Katgun, Satara District of Maharashtra.
 
• **Savitribai Phule,** his wife, is considered the **first female teacher** in India and a leader in the struggle for women's rights.

questions.concept: Advent of Europeans
questions.question: In ______, the British government enacted a legislation banning the use of printed cotton textiles - chintz - in England. Interestingly, this Act was known as the Calico Act.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1720**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1720**, the British government **enacted legislation known as the Calico Act, banning the use of printed cotton textiles - chintz - in England.**
 
• This Act was brought into effect due to the fear that the import of** cheap, colourful, and washable Indian textiles was harming the British wool and silk industries, **which were unable to compete with the more attractive Indian products.
 
• The Calico Act prohibited the use of Indian textiles in Britain, **but they were still allowed for re-export to other places, which ensured the continued operation of the East India Company.**
 
• **The Act illustrates the early impact of global trade and market forces and the measures that governments took to protect their domestic industries.**
 
• Over time, as Britain's own cotton industry developed, the restrictions imposed by the** Calico Act were gradually lifted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calico Act:**

 
 
• The** Calico Act of 1720 **was a piece of protectionist legislation by the British government.
 
• **Calico refers to unbleached, plain-woven cotton textiles, initially imported from India.**
 
• The use of calico from India had become widespread in **England since it was inexpensive, brightly coloured, and considered exotic.**
 
• **The British textile industry felt threatened by the importation of Indian calico.**
 
• To protect its wool and silk industries, the government passed the **Calico Act, banning the use of cotton textiles in England.**
 
• **The Act is a significant indicator of how the British used legislation to control markets and trade in the interests of their home industries.**

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: On 12 August ______, the Mughal emperor appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1765.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **East India Company:- **

 
 
• It was a privately owned company that was established to create profitable trade with countries in the region of Asia called the "East Indies". 
 
• It was granted a Royal Charter by Queen Elizabeth in 1600.
 
• The company was formed to own a stake in the East Indian spice business.
 
• That trade was a monopoly of Spain and Portugal until the defeat of the Spanish Armada (1588) by England gave the British a chance to break the monopoly.
 
• By 1612 the company made separate trips, subscribing separately.
 
• There were temporary joint stocks until 1657 when a permanent joint stock was raised.
 
• On** 12 August 1765 **the Mughal emperor appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.

• The **Battle of Chinhat**, fought on **June 30, 1857**, was a significant early engagement during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• It took place near the town of Chinhat, on the outskirts of **Lucknow**. 
 
• The rebellion against British rule had spread across northern India, and **Lucknow**, the capital of the province of **Oudh (Awadh)**, became a key center of resistance
 
• The **Battle of Chinhat** was a decisive victory for the Indian rebels, and it marked the beginning of the **Siege of Lucknow**.

questions.concept: Advent of Europeans
questions.question: Who led the Battle of Plassey on behalf of the British East India Company?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Robert Clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Battle of Plassey:

 
 
• It was fought in 1757 in the Plassey region of West Bengal, on the east of the Bhagirathi river. 
 
• Troops of the British East India Company, led by Robert Clive, came up against the forces of Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last independent Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• The victory of the British East India Company in the Battle of Plassey is one of the important landmarks in India History. 
 
• The Battle of Plassey paved the way for the beginning of the British empire in India.
 
• The British enjoyed the tax benefits, had to compete with no rival foreign merchants, and began to use the revenue of Bengal for protecting their military and trade interests.
 
• So much wealth was drained from Bengal that the economy was completely shattered. This is known as the Plassey Plunder.
 
• With the wealth of Bengal, the British secured their business and political supremacy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Governor and company of merchants of London trading into the East Indies, popularly known as the English East India Company, were formed in 1600 AD. 
 
• Captain William Hawkins arrived at Jahangir’s court in 1609 AD to seek permission to open a factory in Surat.
 
 
• A Farman was issued by Jahangir, permitting the English to build a factory in Surat.
 
 
 
• In 1613, a permanent factory of East India Company was established at Surat.
 
• In 1611, the company established its first factory in the south in Masulipattanam.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: From which places did Lord Cornwallis start the permanent settlement system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal and Bihar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Permanent Settlement:-**

 
 
• **Lord Cornwallis started the Permanent Settlement system from Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa in 1793. **
 
• It was later extended to other parts of India, including Varanasi and the south district of Madras.
 
• **The Permanent Settlement system was a land revenue system that fixed the amount of land revenue that zamindars, or landlords, had to pay to the British East India Company. **
 
• This system was designed to provide a stable source of revenue for the company and to create a class of loyal landlords who would support British rule.
 
• However, the Permanent Settlement system had a number of negative consequences. **It led to a concentration of land ownership in the hands of a small number of zamindars, and it made it difficult for the government to collect taxes from peasants.**
 
• The system also discouraged investment in agriculture and led to widespread poverty.

questions.concept: Advent of Europeans
questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the East India Company army?

I. Sawar – Men on horses

II. Musket – A heavy gun used by infantry soldiers
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Sawar"** refers to a cavalry **soldier mounted on a horse**.
 
• The East India Company army did have cavalry units composed of soldiers on horseback. ***Hence Statement I is correct.***
 
• The musket was a **widely used firearm** during the time of the East India Company.
 
• It was a** heavy gun** typically carried and operated by infantry soldiers. ***Hence Statement II is also correct.​***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The East India Company was an** English,** and later British, **joint-stock company founded in 1600.**
 
• It was formed to** trade in the Indian Ocean region**, initially with the East Indies, and later with **East Asia.**
 
• In 1600, a group of English businessmen asked **Elizabeth I **for a royal charter that would let their voyage to the East Indies on behalf of the crown in exchange for a **monopoly on trade.**
 
• The merchants put up nearly **70,000 pounds** of their own money to finance the venture, and the **East India Company was born.**

questions.concept: Advent of Europeans
questions.question: In which year did the East-India Company acquire the Diwani of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1765**__.**__​__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa to the East India Company in 1765.
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought between the British and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja Ud Daulah who was the Nawab of Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II.
 
• This battle was won by the Britishers.
 
• The rights were granted by the **Shah Alam-II.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **​****Treaty of Allahabad:**

 
 
• The Treaty of Allahabad was signed on 12 August 1765, between the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II, son of the late Emperor Alamgir II, and Robert Clive, of the East India Company, in the aftermath of the Battle of Buxar of 23 October 1764.
 
• The Treaty marked the political and constitutional involvement and the beginning of British rule in India.
 
• Based on the terms of the agreement, Alam granted the East India Company Diwani rights, or the right to collect taxes on behalf of the Emperor from the eastern province of Bengal-Bihar-Orissa.
 
• These rights allowed the company to collect revenue directly from the people of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which of the following was a feature of the Indian economy before British rule?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Independent economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Independent economy** was a major feature of Indian economy before British rule.
 
• Indian economy was** independent and self-sufficient** before British rule, consisting of various types of **agriculture, handicrafts, and trade.**
 
• India was a major exporter of **various textiles, spices, and other products**, making it a strong and prosperous economy.
 
• Local cottage **industries and handicraft industries** were the backbone of the Indian economy, providing employment in rural and urban areas.
 
• With the advent of British rule, the structure of the Indian economy underwent **significant changes, **making it dependent and vulnerable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During British rule, the Indian economy was **exploited **and restructured to suit British economic interests.
 
• Many **local industries **and **handicrafts **were destroyed or weakened, leading to increased** poverty and unemployment.**
 
• Indian economy became overly dependent on** agriculture,** and farmers were forced to cultivate cash crops, leading to food crisis.
 
• During this period, the development of **manufacturing and industry** in the Indian economy was hampered, and the overall economic condition of the country weakened.
tags: India under East India Company’s Rule

questions.concept: Changes in Indian Administration after 1858
questions.question: Which Act declared that British rule in India would end by 30 June 1948?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Act of 1947.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Act of 1947** is also known as the **Indian Independence Act.**
 
• This Act was passed by the** British Parliament **on **July 18, 1947**, and received royal assent on **July 18, 1947**.
 
• The Act provided for the end of British rule in India and the partition of India into two separate countries,** India and Pakistan.**
 
• The Act also provided for the establishment of two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, within the** British Commonwealth of Nations.**
 
• The Act came into effect on** August 15, 1947, **and marked the **end of British colonial rule **in India after almost **200 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Act of 1858 **is also known as the **Government of India Act**.

 
 
• It transferred the administration of India from the **East India Company to the British Crown**.
 
 
 
• **Act of 1892** is the **Indian Councils Act.**
 
 
• It expanded the** legislative councils **and provided for the election of some members.
 
 
 
• **Act of 1961** is the **Indian Citizenship Act.**
 
 
• **It **provided for the** acquisition and terminatio**n of Indian citizenship.
tags: Changes in Indian Administration after 1858

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: Identify the correctly matched pair of the founder and the social/socio-religious organisation founded.

options.text: Raja Ram Mohan Ray – Arya Samaj

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda – Ramakrishna Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission** is an **Indian socio-religious organization** founded by **Swami Vivekanand on 1 May 1897**. 
 
• It was established in order to propagate the **ideals of Ramakrishna Paramahasa**. 
 
• It conducts research in the field of **health care, elementary and higher education, tribal welfare, and culture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arya Samaj:-**

 
 
• It is the society of **Nobles vigorous reform movement of modern Hinduism**, founded in **1875 by Dayananda Sarasvati.**
 
• **Aim:- ** To reestablish the Vedas, the earliest Hindu scriptures, as revealed truth. 
 
• The Arya Samaj opposes worship of murtis (images), animal sacrifice, shraddha (rituals on behalf of ancestors), basing caste upon birth rather than upon merit, untouchability, child marriage, pilgrimages, priestly craft, and temple offerings. 
 
• It has worked to further **female education and inter caste marriage**, has built missions, orphanages, and homes for widows, has established a network of schools and colleges; and has undertaken famine relief and medical work. 
 
• From its beginning, it was an important factor in the **growth of Indian nationalism**. 
 
 
 
• **Brahmo Samaj:-**
 
 
• It is an atheistic** movement within Hinduism**, founded in **Kolkata in 1828 by Ram Mohan Roy**. 
 
• It does not accept the authority of the Vedas, has no faith in avatars (incarnations), and does not insist on belief in karma (causal effects of past deeds) or samsara (the process of death and rebirth).
 
• It discards Hindu rituals and denounces **polytheism, image worship, and the caste system**.
tags: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Dutch had a monopoly on the spice trade in India in the 17th century.
 
• First Dutch Governor: Pieter Both.
 
• In India they established the first factory in Muslipatnam in 1605, followed by Pulicat in 1610, Surat in 1616, Bimilipatam in 1641, and Chinasurah in 1653.
 
• The factory at Chinasurah was the headquarters for all the Dutch agencies and factories in Bihar, Bengal, Orissa, and Bangladesh.
 
• When they established a factory in Pulicat in 1610 it became their main centre of activities. It was known as Fort Geldria.
 
• The Battle of Bedara(1759) was fought between the English and Dutch armies in Bengal India.
 
• In this battle, the English forces defeated the Dutch Forces and helped the British East India Company to assert their supremacy in India.

• His birthday is celebrated as **national youth day in India.**
 
• **Narendranath Datta** is the original name of Swami Vivekananda.

• "**Go back to Gita**" is a famous slogan raised by Swami Vivekananda.

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Santhal Revolt take place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1855-56.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Santhal Pargana is the mainland of the famous Santhal rebellion. On 30 June 1855, two Santal rebel leaders, Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu** with the help of Chand and Bhairav, mobilized ten thousand Santals and declared a rebellion against British colonists.
 
• Santhal Parganas comprised a district of the same name, in undivided Bihar state, India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Santhal uprising of 1855:**

 
 
• The Santhals were given land and persuaded to settle in the** foothills of Rajmahal.**
 
• By 1832 a large area of land was demarcated as **Damin-i-Koh**. This was declared to be the land of the Santhals. They were to live within it, practice plough agriculture, and become settled peasants.
 
• The land grant to the Santhals stipulated that at least one-tenth of the area was to be cleared and cultivated within the first ten years.
 
• The territory was surveyed and mapped. Enclosed with boundary pillars, it was separated from both the world of the settled agriculturists of the plains and the Paharias of the hills.
 
• After the demarcation of Damin-i-Koh, Santhal settlements expanded rapidly.
 
• From **40 Santhal villages in the area in 1838, as many as 1,473 villages had come up by 1851.**

questions.question: The first cotton textile mill in Ahmedabad was started in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1861.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ahmedabad's first cotton textile mill,** the Ahmedabad Cotton Mill,** started production on **May 30th, 1861.**
 
• It was founded by** Rao Bahadur Ranchhodlal Chhotalal,** an entrepreneur in **Ahmedabad.**** **
 
• It was a spinning factory with** 2,500 spindles** and employed **63 workers. **
 
• It catered to the local handloom weavers' yarn requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** first cotton textile mill in India **was established at** Fort Glastor near Kolkata in 1818.**
 
• **Large-scale production of cotton** started in **Mumbai in 1854.**
 
• **India's first successful mechanized textile mill** was instituted in the **city of Mumbai**, then known as Bombay, in the** year 1854.**
 
• There were several factors that led to the rapid expansion of the industry in the region, the region had **a warm, moist climate that was suitable for the industry.**
